newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cenbank says sees no intervention need - CTK. [CORRECTED 16:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Czech cenbank says sees no intervention need - CTK. [CORRECTED 16:45 GMT]

text.p: A sharp fall in the value of the Czech crown on Monday did not give a reason for the Czech National Bank (CNB) to intervene to prop up its value, the CTK news agency quoted CNB spokesman Martin Svehla as saying.
(Corrects to make clear CNB did NOT see a reason to intervene, adding dropped word).

Quoting Svehla in indirect speech throughout, it said that today's market was very sensitive and the volatility was expected ahead of a government economic stimulus package to be announced on Wednesday.
Svehla pointed out that Monday's central bank fixing fell to just above parity with its dollar/mark basket from +0.80 percent above parity on Friday.
Central bank officials were not available for independent comment on Monday.
The fixing at 1130 local time (0930 gmt) was in-line with market levels at the time, but the crown fell further in afternoon trading to -0.80 percent under parity.
Traders are awaiting the full extent of the cabinet package -- aimed at stemming growing budget and trade deficits and reviving economic growth -- to be announced on Wednesday.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and other senior ministers have suggested a series of budget cuts along with a loosening in monetary policy, but specific details have not been revealed.
The central bank responded last Thursday by easing minimum reserve requriements, but kept key interest rates unchanged.
